title: Kinematics
body:
**Kinematics** describes motion without asking what causes it. Three quantities and the
relationships between them cover the whole topic.

**Displacement** is the change in position, a [[Vector]] pointing from start to finish. It
differs from distance travelled whenever the path bends: a lap of a track has a large distance
and zero displacement.

**Velocity** is the rate of change of displacement, so it is the [[Derivative]] of position and
it is a vector. Speed is its magnitude, which is why average speed and average velocity differ
on a curved path.

**Acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity, the derivative of velocity and the second
derivative of position. Because velocity is a vector, an object accelerates whenever its
direction changes even at constant speed, which is what [[Uniform Circular Motion]]
is.

```
position  x(t)                       metres
velocity  v = dx/dt                  metres per second
accel     a = dv/dt = d²x/dt²        metres per second squared
```

Going the other way, integrating acceleration gives velocity and integrating velocity gives
position, with the constants of integration supplied by the initial conditions. That is where
the equations in [[Uniformly Accelerated Motion]] come from.

A sign convention has to be chosen and then kept. Negative acceleration means speeding up when
the velocity is also negative, so acceleration and deceleration are not the same distinction.
